first: अतुलितबलधामं स्वर्णशैलाभदेहं दनुजवनकृशानुं ज्ञानिनामग्रगण्यम् ।
en: I bow to the Son of the Wind: home of matchless strength, his body shining like a golden mountain, a fire to the forest of demons, foremost among the wise, a store of every virtue, lord of the monkeys, and the chosen messenger of Rama.

first: चौ°-जामवन्त के बचन सुहाये । सुनि हनुमन्त हृदय अति भाये ॥
en: Hanuman was deeply pleased to hear Jambavan's fine words. He said, 'Brothers, bear the hardship, live on roots and fruit, and wait for me here,'

first: जब लगि आवउँ सीतहि देखी। होइ काज मोहि हरष बिसेखी ।।
en: 'until I come back after seeing Sita. The task will succeed, for I feel great joy.' Saying this, he bowed to them all and set off happily, holding Rama in his heart.

first: सिन्धु तीर एक भूधर सुन्दर।कौतुक कूदि चढ़ेउ ता ऊपर ॥
en: On the seashore stood a fine mountain; he leapt onto it in play. Remembering Rama again and again, the mighty Son of the Wind sprang into the air.

first: जेहि गिरि चरन देइ हनुमन्ता । चलेउ सो गा पाताल तुरन्ता ॥
en: Whatever mountain Hanuman pressed with his feet sank at once into the underworld. Like Rama's arrow that never misses, so Hanuman flew on.

first: जलनिधि रघुपति दूत बिचारी । तेैं मैनाक होइ श्रमहारी ॥५॥
en: Seeing that he was Rama's messenger, the Ocean told the mountain Mainaka, 'Rise up and give him a place to rest.'

first: दो॰—हनूमान तेहि परसा,कर पुनि कीन्ह प्रनाम।
en: Hanuman touched the mountain with his hand and bowed to it, saying, 'How can I rest until Rama's work is done?'

first: चौ°—जात पवन सुत देवन्ह देखा।जानइ कहँ बल बुद्धि बिसेखा ॥
en: The gods watched the Son of the Wind go and wanted to test his strength and wisdom. So they sent Surasa, the mother of serpents, who came and spoke to him.

first: आजु सुरन्ह मोहि दीन्ह अहारा।सुनत बचन कहें पवन-कुमारा ॥
en: 'Today the gods have given me my meal.' Hearing this, the Son of the Wind said, 'Let me first do Rama's work, come back, and give my Lord the news of Sita.'

first: तब तव बदन पइठिहौं आई। सत्य कहउँ मोहि जान दे माई।।
en: 'Then I will come and enter your mouth. I tell you truly, mother, let me go.' When she would not let him go by any means, Hanuman said, 'Then why not swallow me?'

first: जोजन भरि तेहि बदन पसारा ।कपि त्तनु कीन्ह दुगुन विस्तारा॥
en: She opened her mouth a league wide, and the monkey made his body twice as large. She made her mouth sixteen leagues, and at once the Son of the Wind became thirty-two.

first: जस जस सुरसा बदन बढ़ावा । तासु दून कपि रूप देखावा ॥
en: However wide Surasa opened her mouth, the monkey showed a form twice as big. When she made her mouth a hundred leagues wide, the Son of the Wind took a very tiny form.

first: बदन पइठि पुनि बाहेर आवा । माँगा बिदा ताहि सिर नावा ॥
en: He entered her mouth and came out again, then bowed his head and asked leave to go. She said, 'I have learned the depth of your wisdom and strength, which is why the gods sent me.'

first: दो॰—रामकाज सब करिहहु, तुम्ह बल-बुद्धि-निधान।
en: 'You will do all of Rama's work, for you are a treasure of strength and wisdom.' She blessed him and left, and Hanuman went on with joy.

first: चौ°—निसिचरि एक सिन्धु मह रहई। करि माया नम के खग गहई ।
en: A demoness lived in the sea who caught birds in the sky by magic. When creatures flew through the air, she looked at their shadows on the water,

first: गहइ छाँह सक से न उड़ाई। एहि बिधि सदा गगन-चर खाई।
en: and seized the shadow, so they could not fly on; in this way she always ate the fliers of the sky. She played the same trick on Hanuman, but the monkey saw through her deceit at once.

first: ताहि मारि मारुत-सुप्त बीरा । बरिधि पार गयउ मतिधीरा
en: The brave, steady-minded Son of the Wind killed her and crossed the sea. There he saw the beauty of the woods, with bees humming, eager for honey.

first: नाना तरु फल फूल सुहाये । खग मृग बृन्द देखि मन भाये ॥
en: Many trees with lovely fruit and flowers, and flocks of birds and herds of deer, delighted his heart. Seeing a great mountain ahead, he ran up it without fear.

first: उमा न कछु कपि कै अधिकाई । प्रभु प्रताप जो कालहि खाई ॥
en: Uma, this was no special greatness of the monkey; it is the glory of the Lord, which devours even Death. From the mountain top he saw Lanka, a fortress beyond words.

first: अति उतङ्ग जलनिधि चहुँ पासा । कनक-कोट कर परम प्रकासा ॥६॥
en: It was very high, with the ocean on all sides, and its wall of gold shone with great brightness.

first: कनक-कोट बिचित्र मनि-कृत, सुन्दरायतना घना।
en: The golden wall was set with many kinds of gems, and inside were many fine houses. There were squares, markets, good roads and lanes; the lovely city was built in every way. Who could count its elephants, horses, mules, foot soldiers and chariots? The hosts of mighty demons in many shapes, and their army, are beyond describing.

first: बन बाग उपबन बाटिका सर, कूप बापी सोहहीं।
en: Woods, gardens, groves, flower beds, lakes, wells and step-wells looked lovely. Daughters of men, Nagas, gods and Gandharvas were so fair they would charm even a sage. Here and there huge wrestlers, big as mountains, roared, fought each other in many arenas, and shouted challenges.

first: करि जतन भट कोटिन्ह बिकट तन, नगर चहुँ दिसि रच्छहीं।
en: Millions of fierce-bodied warriors guarded the city on all four sides with great care. In places the wicked demons were eating buffaloes, humans, cows, donkeys and goats. Tulsidas tells a little of their story because they will surely give up their bodies at the holy bathing place of Rama's arrows and win salvation.

first: दो॰—पुर रखवारे देखि बहु, कपि मन कीन्ह बिचार।
en: Seeing the many guards of the city, the monkey thought, 'I will take a very small form and enter the city at night.'

first: चौ°—मसक समान रूप कपि धरी । लङ्कहि चलेहु सुमिरि नरहरी।
en: The monkey took a form as small as a mosquito and, remembering the Lord in his man-lion form, went towards Lanka. A demoness named Lankini stopped him: 'Where are you going, ignoring me?'

first: जानेहि नहीं मरम सठ मोरा । मोर अहार , जहाँलगि चोरा॥
en: 'Fool, do you not know my secret? Every thief here is my food.' The great monkey struck her with one blow of his fist; she vomited blood and fell rolling on the ground.

first: पुनि सम्भारि उठी सो लङ्का ।जोरि पानि कर बिनय ससङ्का ।
en: Then Lanka recovered and stood up, and folding her hands, spoke humbly and in fear: 'When Brahma gave Ravana his boon, he told me a sign as he left:

first: बिकल होसि तैं कपि के मारे । तब जानेसु निसिचर सङ्घारे ।
en: 'When you are shaken by a monkey's blow, know that the demons are doomed.' Dear one, my merit is very great, for I have seen Rama's messenger with my own eyes.'

first: दो॰—तात स्वर्ग अपबर्ग सुख, धरिय तुला एक अङ्ग।
en: 'Dear one, put the joys of heaven and of final freedom together on one side of a scale; they cannot equal the joy of a single moment in good company.'

first: चौ०-प्रबिसि नगर कीजे सब काजा। हृदय राखि कोसलपुर-राजा॥
en: 'Enter the city and do all your work, keeping the King of Kosala in your heart. For him, poison turns to nectar, an enemy becomes a friend, the ocean shrinks to a cow's hoofprint, and fire turns cool,'

first: गरुअ सुमेरु रेनु सम ताही । राम कृपा करि चितवा जाही ॥
en: 'and huge Mount Sumeru becomes like a speck of dust, for anyone on whom Rama looks with grace.' Hanuman took a very small form and entered the city, remembering the Lord.

first: मन्दिर मन्दिर प्रीति करि सोधा । देखे जहँ तहँ अगनित जोधा ॥
en: He searched every palace with care and saw countless warriors everywhere. He went into Ravana's palace, which was too wonderful to describe.

first: सयन किये देखा कपि तेही । मन्दिर महँ न दीख वैदेही ।
en: The monkey saw Ravana asleep, but he did not see Sita in the palace. Then he saw a lovely house, with a separate temple to Vishnu built in it.

first: दो॰—रामायुध अङ्कित गृह, सेभा बरनि न जाइ ॥
en: The house was marked with Rama's weapons, and its beauty cannot be told. Seeing clusters of fresh tulsi plants there, the monkey king was glad.

first: चौ०- लङ्का निसिचर निकर निवासा । इहाँ कहाँ सज्जन कर बासा ॥
en: 'Lanka is the home of hosts of demons; how can a good man live here?' As the monkey turned this over in his mind, Vibhishana woke up.

first: राम राम तेहि सुमिरन कीन्हा । हृदय हरष कपि सञ्जन चीन्हा ।
en: He began to repeat 'Rama, Rama.' The monkey was glad at heart, knowing him to be a good man. 'I will make myself known to him; no harm can come from a good man.'

first: बिप्र रूप धरि बचन सुनाये । सुनत विभीषन उठि तहँ आये ॥
en: Taking the form of a Brahmin, he called out. Hearing him, Vibhishana rose and came there. He bowed, asked after his welfare, and said, 'Brahmin, tell me your story clearly.'

first: की तुम्ह हरिदासन्ह महँ कोई । मोरे हृदय प्रीति अति हाई ॥
en: 'Are you one of Hari's servants? My heart feels great love for you. Or are you Rama himself, who loves the humble, come to bless me?'

first: दो॰—तब हनुमन्त कही सब,राम कथा निज नाम।
en: Then Hanuman told him all of Rama's story and his own name. As they listened, both thrilled with joy, their minds lost in remembering Rama's virtues.

first: चौ०-सुनहु पवन-सुत रहनि हमारी। जिमि दसनन्हि महँ जीभ बिचारी।
en: 'Hear, Son of the Wind, how I live here: like the poor tongue among the teeth. Dear friend, will the Lord of the Solar race ever see that I am helpless and show me grace?'

first: तामस तनु कछु साधन नाहौँ । प्रीति न पद-सरोज मन माहीं ॥
en: 'My body is full of darkness; I have no spiritual practice, and no love for the Lord's lotus feet in my heart. But now, Hanuman, I have hope, for without Hari's grace one does not meet saints.'

first: जौँ रघुबीर अनुग्रह कीन्हा । तौ तुम्ह मोहि दरस हठि दीन्हा ॥
en: 'Rama must have been kind to me, for you have come to see me of your own will.' Hanuman said, 'Listen, Vibhishana, this is the Lord's way: he always loves his servants.'

first: कहहु कवन मैं परम कुलीना । कपि चञ्चल सबहीं बिधि हीना ॥
en: 'Tell me, how am I of high birth? I am a fickle monkey, lowly in every way. Whoever speaks my name in the morning goes without food that day.'

first: दो॰—अस मैं अधम सखा सुनु,मोहू पर रघुवीर ।
en: 'Listen, friend, even to such a low one as me Rama has shown grace.' Remembering the Lord's goodness, his eyes filled with tears.

first: चौ०-जानतहूँ अस स्वामि विसारी। फिरहिँ ते काहे न होहिँ दुखारी।
en: 'Those who know of such a Master and still forget him and wander off, why should they not suffer?' Talking of Rama's virtues in this way, they found a peace beyond words.

first: पुनि सब कथा बिभीषन कही।जेहि बिधि जनक-सुता तहँ रही ।
en: Then Vibhishana told the whole story of how Janaka's daughter was living there. Hanuman said, 'Listen, brother, I wish to see Mother Janaki.'

first: जुगुति बिभीषन सकल सुनाई ।चलेउ पवन-सुत बिदा कराई। ,
en: Vibhishana explained every means to him, and the Son of the Wind took leave and went. Taking that same tiny form again, he went to the Ashoka grove where Sita was staying.

first: देखि मनहिँ महँ कीन्ह प्रनामा । बैठेहि बीति जात निसि जामा ।
en: Seeing her, he bowed to her in his heart. She sat while the watches of the night slipped by. Her body was thin, her hair was a single matted braid, and in her heart she repeated Rama's virtues.

first: दो॰—निज पद नयन दिये मन, राम-चरन महँ लीन।
en: Her eyes were fixed on her own feet and her mind was absorbed in Rama's feet. Seeing Janaki so wretched, the Son of the Wind was deeply grieved.

first: चौ°—तरु पल्लव महँ रहा लुकाई। करइ विचार करउँ का भाई ॥
en: He stayed hidden among the leaves of a tree, thinking, 'What should I do now?' Just then Ravana came there with many women, all dressed up.

first: बहु बिधि खल सीतहि समुझावा ।साम दाम भय भेद देखावा ।
en: The wicked one tried to win Sita over in many ways, using sweet talk, bribes, threats and division. Ravana said, 'Listen, fair and wise one: Mandodari and all my queens'

first: तव अनुचरी करउँ पन मोरा । एक बार बिलोकु मम ओरा ॥
en: 'I will make your servants, I promise, if you will look at me just once.' Holding a blade of grass between herself and him, Sita spoke, remembering her most loving Lord of Avadh:

first: सुनु दसमुख खद्योत प्रकासा । कबहुँ कि नलिनी करइ बिकासा ।
en: 'Listen, ten-headed one: can the lotus ever open in the light of a firefly? Think this over in your mind,' said Janaki. 'Wicked one, you have forgotten Rama's arrows.'

first: सठ सूने हरि आनेहि मोही ।अधम निलज्ज लाज नहिँ तोही ॥५॥
en: 'Rascal, you carried me off when he was away. Vile, shameless one, have you no shame?'

first: दो॰—आपुहि सुनि खद्योत सम,रामहिँ भानु समान ।
en: Hearing himself called a firefly and Rama the sun, and hearing her harsh words, he drew his sword and spoke in great anger:

first: चौ०-सीता तैं मम कृत अपमाना। कटिहउँ तवसिर कठिन कृपाना॥
en: 'Sita, you have insulted me; I will cut off your head with my hard sword. Or else obey me at once. Fair one, if not, you will lose your life.'

first: स्याम-सरोज-दाम सम सुन्दर । प्रभु भुज करि कर सम दसकन्धर ॥
en: Sita said, 'My Lord's arm is lovely like a garland of dark lotuses, long like an elephant's trunk, ten-headed one. Either that arm will be round my neck, or your terrible sword. Listen, rascal, this is my true vow.'

first: त्रिजटा नाम राक्षसी एका। राम चरन-रति निपुन बिबेका॥
en: There was a demoness named Trijata who loved Rama's feet and was wise in judgment. She called all the others and told them her dream: 'Serve Sita and do yourselves good.'

first: चन्द्रहास हर मम परितापं। रघुपति-बिरह-अनल सज्जातं ।
en: 'O sword Chandrahas, take away my pain, born of the fire of separation from Rama. You are cool, sharp, with a fine edge,' said Sita. 'Remove my heavy sorrow.'

first: सुनत बचन पुनि मारन धावा । मय-तनया कहि नीति बुझावा ॥
en: Hearing this, he rushed again to kill her, but Mandodari, daughter of Maya, calmed him with wise counsel. Then he called all the demonesses and told them to go and frighten Sita in every way.

first: मास-दिवस महँ कहा न माना । तौ मैं मारब काढ़ि कृपाना ॥
en: 'If she does not obey me within a month, I will draw my sword and kill her.'

first: दो॰—भवन गयउ दसकन्धर, इहाँ पिसाचिनि बृन्द ।
en: The ten-headed one went back to his palace. Here a crowd of demonesses took many ugly forms and frightened Sita.

first: चौ°—त्रिजटा नाम राक्षसी एका । राम चरन रति निपुन बिबेका ॥
en: There was a demoness named Trijata who loved Rama's feet and was wise in judgment. She called all the others and told them her dream: 'Serve Sita and do yourselves good.'

first: सपने बानर लङ्का जारी । जातुधान सेना सब मारी ॥
en: 'In my dream a monkey burned Lanka and killed the whole demon army. Ravana was naked, riding a donkey, with his heads shaven and his twenty arms cut off.'

first: एहि बिधि सो दच्छिंन दिसि जाई। लङ्का मनहुँ बिभीषन पाई।
en: 'In this state he went off to the south, and it seemed Vibhishana had got Lanka. Rama's rule was proclaimed through the city, and then the Lord sent for Sita.'

first: यह सपना मैं कहऊँ पुकारी । होइहि सत्य गये दिन चारी।
en: 'I say this aloud: this dream will come true in a few days.' Hearing her words, they all grew afraid and fell at the feet of Janaka's daughter.

first: दो॰—जहँ तहँ गई सकल मिलि, सीता कर मन सोच ।
en: They all went off here and there. Sita worried in her mind: 'When the month is over, the vile demon will kill me.'

first: चौ°—त्रिजटा सन बाली करजोरी। मातु बिपति सङ्गिनि तैँ मोरी ॥
en: Folding her hands, she said to Trijata, 'Mother, you are my companion in trouble. Quickly find a way for me to leave this body; I can no longer bear this separation.'

first: आनि काठ रचु चिता बनाई। मातु अनल पुनि देहि लगाई।
en: 'Bring wood and build a pyre, mother, then set it on fire. Wise one, prove my love true. Who can bear to hear his words, which pierce the ears like spears?'

first: सुनत बचन पद गहि समुझायेसि । प्रभु प्रताप-बल-सुजस सुनायेसि ।
en: Hearing this, Trijata held her feet and comforted her, telling of the Lord's glory, strength and fame. 'Listen, gentle one, no fire can be had at night.' Saying this, she went home.

first: कह सीता बिधि भा प्रतिकूला । मिलिहि न पावक मिटिहि न सूला ॥
en: Sita said, 'Fate is against me. I will find no fire, and my pain will not end. I can see sparks of fire in the sky, yet not one star comes down to earth.'

first: पावकमय ससि स्रवत न आगी । मानहुँ
en: 'The moon is made of fire, yet it lets none fall, as if it knows how unlucky I am. Ashoka tree, hear my prayer: make your name true and take away my grief.'

first: नूतन किसलय अनल समाना । देहि अगिनि तन करहि निदाना ॥
en: 'Your fresh red leaves are like fire; give me fire and end this body.' Seeing Sita so tormented by separation, that moment felt like an age to the monkey.

first: सो°-कपि करि हृदय बिचार, दीन्हि मुद्रिका डारि तब ।
en: Then the monkey thought it over and dropped the ring. It was as if the Ashoka tree had given her a spark; she rose with joy and took it in her hand.

first: चौ°—तब देखी मुद्रिका मनोहर । राम-नाम-अंकित अति सुन्दर ॥
en: She saw the charming ring, very beautiful, engraved with Rama's name. She stared in wonder and knew the ring; her heart was troubled with both joy and grief.

first: जीति को सकइ अजय रघुराई । माया तें असि रचि नहिं जाई ।
en: 'Who can defeat Rama, who is never defeated? And such a ring cannot be made by magic.' As Sita thought many such things, Hanuman spoke in a sweet voice.

first: रामचन्द्र गुन बरनइ लागा। सुनतहि सीता कर दुख भागा ॥
en: He began to describe Rama's virtues, and as Sita heard them her sorrow fled. She listened with all her heart, and he told the whole story from the start.

first: स्रवनामृत जेहि कथा सुनाई ।कहिं सो प्रगट होत किन भाई ॥
en: 'Brother, you who told me this story, sweet as nectar to the ears, why do you not show yourself?' Then Hanuman went up close to her. She turned away and sat, surprised in her mind.

first: राम-दूत मैं मातु जानकी। सत्य सपथ करुनानिधान की ॥
en: 'Mother Janaki, I am Rama's messenger; I swear by the ocean of mercy. Mother, I have brought this ring; Rama gave it as a token for you.'

first: नर बानरहि सङ्ग कहु कैसे । कही कथा भइ सङ्गति जैसे ॥६॥
en: 'Tell me how men and monkeys came together.' He told her the story of how their friendship came about.

first: दो॰—कपि के बचन सप्रेम सुनि, उपजा मन विस्वास।
en: Hearing the monkey's loving words, she came to trust him. She knew he was a servant of the merciful Lord in thought, deed and word.

first: चौ°—हरिजन जांनि प्रीति अति बाढ़ी। सजल नयन पुलकावलि ठाढ़ी।
en: Knowing him to be the Lord's servant, her love grew greatly; her eyes filled with tears and her body thrilled. 'Hanuman, I was drowning in a sea of separation, and you have become my boat, dear one.'

first: अब कहु कुसल जाउँ बलिहारी । अनुज सहित सुख-भवन-खरारी ।
en: 'Bless you, now tell me: is Rama, the home of joy, well along with his brother? Rama is tender-hearted and kind; why, monkey, has he become so hard?'

first: सहज बानि सेवक सुखदायक । कबहुँक सुरति करत रघुनायक ॥
en: 'It is his nature to bring joy to his servants. Does Rama ever remember me? Will my eyes ever be soothed, dear one, by seeing his dark, soft body?'

first: बचन न आव नयन भरि बारी । अहह नाथ हौँ निपट बिसारी ॥
en: No words came, and her eyes filled with tears: 'Ah Lord, you have quite forgotten me!' Seeing Sita so tormented by separation, the monkey spoke soft and humble words:

first: मातु कुसल प्रभु अनुज समेता । तव दुख दुखी सुकृपा-निकेता।।
en: 'Mother, the Lord and his brother are well, but the merciful one grieves at your grief. Do not think yourself less loved, mother; Rama's love is twice what yours is.'

first: दो०-रघुपति कर सन्देस अब, सुनु जननी धरि धीर।
en: 'Mother, now be calm and hear Rama's message.' Saying this, the monkey choked with feeling and his eyes filled with tears.

first: चौ°—कहेउ राम बियोग तव सीता। मो कह सकल भये बिपरीता।
en: 'Rama said: Sita, since I lost you, everything has turned against me. The fresh leaves of the trees feel like fire, the night like the night of doom, the moon like a burning sun,'

first: कुबलय विपिन कुन्त बन सरिसा । बारिद तपत तेल जनु वरिसा ।
en: 'the lotus beds like a forest of spears, and the clouds seem to rain boiling oil. Things that used to comfort me now cause pain, and the cool, soft, fragrant breeze is like a snake's breath.'

first: कहेहू तेँ कछु दुख घटि होई । काहि कहउँ यह जान न कोई ।
en: 'Telling one's sorrow eases it a little, but whom can I tell? No one understands. Only my mind knows the truth of the love between you and me, my dear,'

first: सो मन सदा रहत तोहि पाहीं । जानु प्रीति रस एतनेहिँ माहीँ ।
en: 'and that mind stays always with you. Know the essence of my love from this alone.' Hearing the Lord's message, Sita was so lost in love that she forgot her body.

first: कह कपि हृदय धीर धरु माता । सुमिरु राम सेवक-सुख दाता ॥
en: The monkey said, 'Mother, take heart. Remember Rama, who brings joy to his servants. Bring Rama's might to mind, listen to me, and give up your fear.'

first: दो०-निसिचर निकर पतङ्ग सम, रघुपति बान कृसानु ।
en: 'The hosts of demons are like moths and Rama's arrows like fire. Mother, take heart, and know the demons already burned.'

first: चौ°—जौँ रघुबीर होति सुधि पाई । करते नहिँ बिलम्ब रघुराई ।
en: 'Had Rama received news of you, he would not have delayed. Janaki, when the sun of Rama's arrows rises, where will the darkness of the demon hordes be?'

first: अबहिं मातु मैँ जाउँ लेवाई। प्रभु आयसु नहिं राम-दोहाई ॥
en: 'Mother, I could take you away right now, but I swear by Rama, I do not have the Lord's order. Mother, be patient a few more days; Rama will come with the monkeys,'

first: निसिचर मारि तोहि लेइ जइहहिँ । तिहुँ पुर नारदादि जस गइहहिं ।
en: 'kill the demons and take you away, and Narada and others will sing his fame in the three worlds.' Sita said, 'Son, are all the monkeys as small as you? The demon warriors are very strong.'

first: मोरे हृदय परम सन्देहा । सुनि कपि प्रगट कीन्हि निज देहा।
en: 'My heart has a great doubt.' Hearing this, the monkey showed his true body: huge as a golden mountain, terrible in battle, and of great strength and courage.

first: सीता मन भरोस तब भयऊ । पुनि लघु रूप पवन-सुत लयऊ ॥३॥
en: Then Sita's mind was put at ease, and the Son of the Wind took a small form again.

first: दो०-सुनु माता साखामृग, नहिँ बल-बुद्धि बिसाल ।
en: 'Listen, mother: monkeys do not have great strength or wisdom. But by the Lord's glory, a very small snake can eat even Garuda.'

first: चौ०-मन सन्तोष सुनत कपि बानी। भगति-प्रताप-तेज-बल-सानी ॥
en: Sita was content to hear the monkey's words, full of devotion, glory, power and strength. Knowing him dear to Rama, she blessed him: 'Son, be a treasure of strength and good conduct.'

first: अजर अमर गुन-निधि सुत होहू । करहिं बहुत रघुनायक छोहू ॥
en: 'Son, may you never grow old or die, and be a treasure of virtues; may Rama shower his love on you.' When Hanuman heard 'may the Lord be kind to you,' he was lost in deep love.

first: बार बार नायेसि पद सीसा । बोला बचन जोरि कर कीसा ।
en: Again and again the monkey bowed his head at her feet and spoke with folded hands: 'Mother, now my life is fulfilled; your blessing is known never to fail.'

first: सुनहु मातु मोहि अतिसयं भूखा । लागि देखि सुन्दर फल रूखा ॥
en: 'Listen, mother, I am very hungry, seeing these trees with lovely fruit.' 'Listen, son, very strong and fierce demons guard this grove.'

first: तिन्ह कर भय माता माहि नाहींँ । जौँ तुम्ह सुख मानहु मन माहीं ॥५॥
en: 'Mother, I have no fear of them, if only you are pleased in your heart.'

first: दो॰—देखि बुद्धि-बल-निपुन कपि, कहेउ जानकी जाहु ।
en: Seeing the monkey skilled in wisdom and strength, Janaki said, 'Go, son. Keep Rama's feet in your heart and eat the sweet fruit.'

first: चौ०-चलेउ नाइ सिर पैठेउ बागा। फल खायेसि तरु तारइ लागा ॥
en: He bowed his head, went and entered the garden. He ate the fruit and began breaking the trees. Many warriors guarded the place; he killed some, and some went and cried for help.

first: नाथ एक आवा कपि भारी। तेहि असोकबाटिका उजारी ॥
en: 'Lord, a huge monkey has come and wrecked the Ashoka grove. He has eaten the fruit, torn up the trees, and crushed the guards to the ground.'

first: सुनि रावन पठये भट नाना । तिन्हहिँ देखि गर्जेउ हनुमाना ।
en: Hearing this, Ravana sent many warriors. Seeing them, Hanuman roared. The monkey killed all the demons, and some ran off half dead, crying out.

first: पुनि पठयेउ तेहि अछयकुमारा । चला सङ्गः लै सुभट अपारा॥
en: Then Ravana sent Prince Akshaya, who set out with countless fine warriors. Seeing him come, Hanuman grabbed a tree and challenged him, struck him down, and roared with a mighty voice.

first: दो०-कछु मारेसि कछु मर्देसि, कछु मिलयेसि धरि धूरि ।
en: Some he killed, some he crushed, and some he caught and rubbed into the dust. Some went back crying, 'Lord, the monkey is very strong!'

first: चौ०-सुनि सुत बध लंकेस रिसाना । पठयेसि मेघनाद बलवाना ॥
en: Hearing of his son's death, Ravana was furious and sent mighty Meghanada: 'Do not kill him, son; tie him up. Let us see this monkey and where he comes from.'

first: चला इन्द्रजित अतुलित्त जोधा । बन्धु निधन सुनि उपजा क्रोधा ॥
en: Indrajit, the matchless warrior, set out, angry at hearing of his brother's death. The monkey saw a fierce warrior coming, gnashed his teeth, roared and rushed at him.

first: अति बिसाल तरु एक उपारा । बिरथ कीन्ह लंकेसकुमारा।
en: He tore up a huge tree and smashed Ravana's son's chariot, leaving him without one. The great warriors with Indrajit he seized one by one and crushed with his body.

first: तिन्हहिं निपाति ताहि सन बाजा । भिरे जुगल मानहुँ गजराजा ॥
en: After killing them he fought Indrajit himself; the two clashed like two great elephants. Striking him with his fist, the monkey climbed a tree, and Indrajit fainted for a moment.

first: उठि बहोरि कीन्हेसि बहु माया । जीति न जाइ प्रभंजन-माया ॥५॥
en: He rose again and used many magic tricks, but the Son of the Wind could not be beaten.

first: दो॰—ब्रह्म-अस्त्र तेहि साधा, कपि मन कीन्ह विचार।
en: He then aimed Brahma's weapon. The monkey thought, 'If I do not honour Brahma's weapon, its great glory will be lost.'

first: चौ°—ब्रह्मबान कपि कहँ तेहि मारा। परतिहु बार कटक सङ्घारा ॥
en: He struck the monkey with Brahma's arrow; even as he fell, Hanuman crushed part of the army. When Indrajit saw the monkey had fainted, he bound him with a serpent noose and carried him off.

first: जासु नाम जपि सुनहु भवानी। भव-बन्धन काटहिं नर ज्ञानी ।
en: Listen, Bhavani: by repeating his name, wise men cut the bonds of worldly life. Could his messenger ever be bound? To serve his Lord's purpose, the monkey let himself be tied.

first: कपि-बन्धन सुनि निसिचर धाये । कौतुक लागि सभा सब आये ॥
en: Hearing that the monkey was bound, the demons ran to the court to watch the sight. The monkey saw Ravana's court; its splendour was beyond words.

first: कर जोरे सुर दिलिप विनीता। भृकुटि बिलोकत सकल सभीता ॥
en: Gods and kings stood humbly with folded hands, all fearfully watching Ravana's brows. Seeing such power, the monkey felt no fear, like Garuda fearless among snakes.

first: दो॰—कपिहि बिलोकि दसानन, विहँसा कहि दुर्बाद ।
en: Seeing the monkey, Ravana laughed and spoke insults. Then he remembered his son's death, and grief rose in his heart.

first: चौ°—कह लङ्केस कवन तैँ कीसा । केहि के बल घालेहि बन खीसा ।।
en: The lord of Lanka said, 'Who are you, monkey? By whose strength did you ruin my grove? Have you never heard of me? I see you are a very bold rascal.'

first: मारे निसिचर केहि अपराधा । कहु सठ तोहि न प्रान कै बाधा ॥
en: 'For what fault did you kill the demons? Tell me, fool, do you not fear for your life?' Hanuman said, 'Listen, Ravana: he by whose strength Maya creates all the countless worlds,'

first: जाके बल विरंचि हरि ईसा । पालत सृजत हरत दससीसा ।
en: 'by whose strength Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva create, preserve and destroy, ten-headed one; by whose strength the thousand-headed serpent holds on his head the universe with its mountains and forests;'

first: धरइ जो विविध देह सुर-त्राता । तुम्ह से सठन्ह सिखावनदाता ॥
en: 'who takes many forms to protect the gods and teaches lessons to fools like you; who broke Shiva's hard bow, and with it crushed the pride of all the kings, you included;'

first: खर दूषन त्रिसिरा अरु बाली । बधे सकल अतुलित बल-साली ॥२॥
en: 'who killed Khara, Dushana, Trishira and Vali, all of matchless strength;'

first: दो॰—जाके बल लवलेस तैं, जितेहु चराचर झारि ।
en: 'by a tiny part of whose strength you conquered all the world, moving and unmoving; I am the messenger of him whose dear wife you carried off.'

first: चौ०-जानउँ मैं तुम्हारि प्रभुताई। सहसबाहु. सनः परी लराई ॥
en: Hanuman said, 'I know your might: you fought with Sahasrabahu, and won fame fighting Vali.' Hearing the monkey's words, Ravana laughed them off.

first: खायेउँ फल प्रभु लागी भूखा। कपि सुभाव तेँ तारेउँ रूखा ॥
en: 'Lord, I ate the fruit because I was hungry, and broke the trees because it is a monkey's nature. Master, everyone loves their own body; those evil ones attacked me,'

first: जिन्ह मोहि मारा ते मैं मारे। तेहि पर बाँधेउ तनय तुम्हारे ॥
en: 'so I struck those who struck me. Then your son tied me up. I feel no shame at being bound; I only want to do my Lord's work.'

first: बिनती करउँ जोरि कर रावन । सुनहु मान तजि मोर सिखावन ॥
en: 'Ravana, I beg you with folded hands: give up your pride and hear my advice. Think of your own family, give up your delusion, and worship him who removes the fears of his devotees.'

first: जाके डर अति काल डेराई । जो सुर असुर चराचर खाई ॥
en: 'Even Death, who eats gods, demons and all creatures, is terrified of him. Never make an enemy of him. Take my advice and give back Janaki.'

first: दो०-प्रनतपाल रघुनायक, करुनासिन्धु खरारि ।
en: 'Rama protects those who bow to him; he is an ocean of mercy, the slayer of Khara. If you go to him for shelter, the Lord will forget your wrongs and protect you.'

first: चौ०-राम चरन-पङ्कज उर धरहू । लङ्का अचल राज तुम्ह करहू ।
en: 'Keep Rama's lotus feet in your heart and rule Lanka forever. The fame of the sage Pulastya is like the spotless moon; do not be a stain on that moon.'

first: राम नाम बिनु गिरा न सोहा । देखु बिचारि त्यागि मद मोहा ॥
en: 'Speech does not shine without Rama's name; think it over and give up pride and delusion. Enemy of the gods, a fine woman wearing every jewel does not look beautiful without clothes.'

first: राम बिमुख सम्पति प्रभुताई । जाइ रही पाई बिनु पाई ॥
en: 'Wealth and power turned away from Rama are lost; having them is like not having them. Rivers that have no springs at their source dry up as soon as the rains are over.'

first: सुनु दसकंठ कहउँ पन रोपी । बिमुख राम त्राता नहिँ कोपी ।
en: 'Listen, ten-headed one, I promise you: no one can save the one who turns from Rama. A thousand Shivas, Vishnus and Brahmas cannot protect you if you are Rama's enemy.'

first: दो॰—मोह मूल बहु सूल प्रद, त्यागहु तम अमिमान ।
en: 'Give up dark pride, the root of delusion and the cause of much pain. Worship Rama, Lord of the Raghus, the ocean of mercy, God himself.'

first: चौ०-जदपिकहीकपिअतिहितबानी। भगति-बिबेक-बिरति-नय-सानी।
en: Though the monkey spoke very kind words, full of devotion, wisdom, detachment and good sense, the very proud Ravana laughed and said, 'I have found a monkey for a great wise teacher!'

first: मृत्यु निकट आई खल तोही ।लागेसि अधम सिखावन मोही।
en: 'Wicked one, your death is near, that you, a low creature, try to teach me.' Hanuman said, 'It will be the opposite; I can clearly see your mind is confused.'

first: सुनि कपि बचन बहुत खिसियाना । बेगि न हरहु मूढ़ कर प्राना ।
en: Hearing the monkey's words, he grew very angry: 'Quick, why do you not take this fool's life?' Hearing this, the demons rushed to kill him, but Vibhishana came with ministers.

first: नाइ सीस करि बिनय बहूता । नीति विरोध न मारिय दूता॥
en: He bowed his head and pleaded: 'Killing an envoy is against the rules of conduct. Master, give him some other punishment.' Everyone said, 'Brother, that is good advice.'

first: सुनत बिहँसि बोला दसकन्धर । अङ्गभङ्ग करि पठवहु बन्दर ॥३॥
en: Hearing this, Ravana laughed and said, 'Then cripple the monkey and send him back.'

first: दो॰—कपि के ममता पूँछि पर, सबहि कहेउ समुझाइ ।
en: He explained to them all, 'A monkey loves its tail. Soak cloth in oil, tie it round his tail, and set it on fire.'

first: चौ०-पूँछ हीनबानर तहँ जाइहि । तब सठ निज नाथहि लेइ आइहि ॥
en: 'When the tailless monkey goes back, the fool will bring his master here. Then I will see the might of the one he has praised so much.'

first: बचन सुनत कपि मन मुसुकाना । भइ सहाइ सारद मैं जाना ।
en: Hearing this, the monkey smiled to himself: 'I see that Saraswati, goddess of speech, has helped me.' Hearing Ravana's order, the foolish demons began to carry it out.

first: रहा न नगर बसन घृत तेला। बाढ़ी पूँछि कीन्ह कपि खेला॥
en: No cloth, ghee or oil was left in the city, for the monkey played a trick and made his tail grow longer and longer. The townspeople came to watch, kicking him and laughing a lot.

first: बाजहिँ ढोल देहिँ सब तारी। नगर, फेरि पुनि पूँछि प्रजारी ॥
en: Drums beat and everyone clapped. They paraded him through the city, then set his tail on fire. When Hanuman saw the fire burning, he at once took a very small form,

first: निबुकि चढ़ेउ कपि कनक अटारी । भई सभीत निसाचर-नारीं ॥५॥
en: slipped free, and jumped onto the golden roofs. The demon women were filled with fear.

first: दो॰—-हरि-प्रेरित तेहि अवसर, चले मरुत उनचास ।
en: At that moment, moved by the Lord, all forty-nine winds began to blow. The monkey laughed aloud, roared, and grew until he touched the sky.

first: चौ०-देह बिसाल परम हरुआई। मन्दिर तेँ मन्दिर चढ़ धाई ॥
en: His body was huge yet very light; he ran from palace to palace. The city burned and the people were in despair, as countless terrible flames leapt out.

first: तात मात हा सुनिय पुकारा । एहि अवसर को हमहिँ उबारा ॥
en: Cries were heard: 'Oh father! Oh mother! Who will save us now? Didn't we say this was no monkey, but some god in a monkey's form?'

first: साधु अवज्ञा कर फल ऐसा । जरइ नगर अनाथ कर जैसा ।।
en: 'This is the fruit of insulting a holy man: the city burns as if it had no master.' He burned the city in a moment; only Vibhishana's house was spared.

first: ता कर दूत अनले जेहि सिरजा। जरा न सो तेहि कारन गिरजा ।।
en: Girija, he did not burn because he was the messenger of the one who created fire. Turning this way and that, he burned all of Lanka, then jumped into the sea.

first: दो०-पूँछि बुझाइ खोइ खम, धरि लघुरूप बहोरि ।
en: He put out his tail, rested from his effort, took a small form again, and stood before Janaka's daughter with folded hands.
